title: Pharmacist Salary Perth: Award Rates and How to Calculate Your Annual Pay
description: Discover the minimum pharmacist salary perth under the Pharmacy Industry Award. Learn to convert hourly rates to annual pay, including tax and superannuation.
salarySummary: The minimum hourly rate for a pharmacist under the Pharmacy Industry Award is $41.74, giving an annual salary of about $82,476 for a 38-hour week before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a pharmacist in Perth?
faqs.a: Under the Pharmacy Industry Award 2020, the minimum hourly rate for a pharmacist is $41.74 (from 1 July 2026). This applies nationally, including Perth. For an experienced pharmacist, the rate is $45.72 per hour, and a pharmacist manager earns $52.15 per hour. These are the base rates for full-time and part-time employees.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours per week (usually 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $41.74 × 38 × 52 = $82,476.64. This is your gross annual salary before tax and super. You can use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site to do the calculation.

faqs.q: Does the award rate include casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The award rates in Table 3 are minimum rates for full-time and part-time employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a casual pharmacist, the rate would be $41.74 × 1.25 = $52.18 per hour. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this works.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you are looking for a **pharmacist salary perth** figure, the starting point is the Pharmacy Industry Award 2020. This award sets the minimum pay rates for pharmacists and pharmacy assistants across Australia, including Western Australia. The rates are updated each year following the Annual Wage Review. From 1 July 2026, the minimum hourly rate for a pharmacist is $41.74, as published by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

This article explains how to convert that hourly rate into an annual salary, what tax and Medicare levy you can expect, and how superannuation is paid on top. The figures here are estimates based on the award and the 2026–27 tax year. For a personalised calculation, use the [timesheet](/) on this site.

## How to Calculate Your Annual Pharmacist Salary

The standard full-time week under the Pharmacy Industry Award is 38 ordinary hours. To find your gross annual salary, use the formula:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a pharmacist on the minimum rate:

$41.74 × 38 × 52 = $82,476.64 per year

If you are an experienced pharmacist ($45.72/hour), the annual figure is:

$45.72 × 38 × 52 = $90,342.72

And for a pharmacist manager ($52.15/hour):

$52.15 × 38 × 52 = $103,048.40

These amounts are before tax, before super, and before any deductions. They assume you work exactly 38 hours every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. If you work part-time, adjust the hours per week accordingly. For example, a part-time pharmacist working 30 hours per week at $41.74/hour would earn $41.74 × 30 × 52 = $65,114.40.

You can also think in fortnights: multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time pharmacist, weekly pay is $41.74 × 38 = $1,586.12, so fortnightly pay is $3,172.24. This is useful if you are paid fortnightly.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Pharmacist Salary

Once you have your gross annual salary, you need to estimate the tax you will pay. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) uses a progressive tax scale for residents. For 2026–27, the tax brackets are:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay the Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The Medicare levy surcharge (for singles without private hospital cover) may also apply if your income exceeds $93,000, but that is not included in this estimate.

Using the minimum pharmacist salary of $82,476:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201–$45,000 (26,800): 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001–$82,476 (37,476): 30% = $11,242.80
- Total tax: $15,262.80
- Medicare levy (2% of $82,476): $1,649.52
- Total tax and Medicare: $16,912.32
- Net annual take-home: $82,476 – $16,912.32 = $65,563.68

For an experienced pharmacist earning $90,342:

- Tax: $0 + $4,020 + 30% of ($90,342 – $45,000 = $45,342) = $13,602.60 → total $17,622.60
- Medicare: $1,806.84
- Total deductions: $19,429.44
- Net: $70,912.56

These are estimates. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page on this site can help you run your own numbers.

## Superannuation on Top

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your salary, not deducted from it. Under the Superannuation Guarantee, the rate from 1 July 2026 is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

For a minimum-rate pharmacist:

- Super contribution: 12% of $82,476 = $9,897.12 per year
- Total cost to employer: $82,476 + $9,897.12 = $92,373.12

Your super is invested and generally not accessible until retirement. If you salary-sacrifice additional amounts, that can reduce your taxable income, but that is not covered here. See the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

## Casual and Part-Time Considerations

If you work as a casual pharmacist, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. That means $41.74 × 1.25 = $52.18 per hour. The casual loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. For a casual working 38 hours, the annual equivalent would be $52.18 × 38 × 52 = $103,107.68, but casuals often work fewer hours. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains the rules.

Part-time pharmacists are paid the same minimum hourly rate as full-time employees, but work fewer hours. Their entitlements (leave, penalty rates) are pro-rated.

## Using the Award Rates for Perth

The Pharmacy Industry Award applies nationally, so the rates are the same in Perth as in Sydney or Melbourne. However, some employers may pay above the award, especially for experienced pharmacists or those in charge. The Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guide provides a full summary of rates including penalty rates for evening, Saturday, and Sunday work. If you work those hours, your actual pay will be higher than the base rate.

Remember that this article provides estimates only. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site to calculate your own annual salary based on your actual hourly rate and hours.
